turns.prompt: Now run a PCA and tell me how many components explain 80% of variance

calls.name: r

input.code:
pca = prcomp(t(norm[apply(norm, 1, var) > 0, ]), scale. = TRUE)
ve = cumsum(pca$sdev^2) / sum(pca$sdev^2)
which(ve >= 0.8)[1]
round(ve[1:6], 3)

turns.prompt: Plot PC1 against PC2 coloured by batch

calls.name: r

input.code:
samples = data.table::fread("data/samples.csv")
pc = data.frame(pca$x[, 1:2], batch = samples$batch[match(rownames(pca$x), samples$sample)])
p_pca = ggplot2::ggplot(pc, ggplot2::aes(PC1, PC2, colour = batch)) + ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) + ggplot2::theme_minimal()
p_pca
